name: Hydroxyethylurea

lead: Hydroxyethylurea is a small, water-loving molecule related to urea. In skincare it is listed as hydroxyethyl urea and works as a humectant and skin-conditioning agent, attracting and holding water in the outer layer of skin.
The appearance payoff is softer, hydrated-feeling skin and a lightweight, non-tacky texture in creams, serums and hair products.

paras: It is an ingredient in leave-on moisturizers, serums and hair-care products rather than a product on its own. Ingredient suppliers describe formula levels from about 1 to 20 percent.

Supplier and brand descriptions call it generally low-irritation, though some note it may sting on severely compromised skin. The Cosmetic Ingredient Review panel published a 2024 safety assessment of it for cosmetic use.

angle.text: Used in moisturizers, hydroxyethylurea helps skin hold water, which gives a soft, hydrated look and feel without greasiness.

lead: Hydroxyethylurea (hydroxyethyl urea) is a synthetic humectant used in skincare and hair care. Supplier and brand pages describe it as drawing moisture into the outer layer of skin, supporting the skin barrier and feeling lighter and less tacky than glycerin.
A 2024 Cosmetic Ingredient Review safety assessment is the main review of its cosmetic use.

Most published work using the same name is unrelated to skincare, such as studies of water-desalination membranes that use hydroxyethylurea units, and older toxicology studies of nitrosated derivatives, which are different compounds. [1]

paras: Brand and supplier descriptions position it as a hydrating ingredient in leave-on products and as a lighter-feeling alternative to glycerin.
No studies found on cosmetic use beyond the safety assessment. Other literature using the name concerns materials science. [1]
